PullRequest.Title: debug: read/write memory support
PullRequest.Body:
This implements the core memory "model" for debugging that reflects
DAP, in `debugModel.ts`. It also implements a filesystem provider based
on that in `debugMemory.ts`, for application in the hex editor.

Finally it adds context menu items for these. This works with changes in
mock debug and https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-hexeditor/pull/309

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The changed render path, row disposal ownership, and Menu's global registry subscription are all explicit in repository code. Virtualization bounds simultaneous rows but not leaked menus across render lifecycles; only the exact growth rate depends on user stepping and scrolling frequency.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Menu instances, their MenuRegistry event subscriptions, overlay context maps, and rebuild schedulers
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Retention grows by one menu for every rendered variable-row lifecycle; repeated debugger stops, variable refreshes, and scrolling continuously add menus even though the tree virtualizes rows.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: steadily increasing retained heap and GC pressure during long debugging sessions, plus fan-out rebuilding every leaked menu when the variables menu registry changes
Findings.PreviousBehavior: VariablesView created one DebugVariablesContext menu in its constructor and registered that single menu with the view lifecycle for disposal.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Every VariablesRenderer.renderActionBar call now creates a new menu for that row, but elementDisposable receives only the actions returned by createAndFillInContextMenuActions; the menu itself is never disposed when disposeElement recycles the row.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The added `const menu = this.menuService.createMenu(...)` at line 433 moves menu creation from one view-owned instance to each row render, while the following added push stores only `createAndFillInContextMenuActions(...)` in `data.elementDisposable`.
Findings.Title: Dispose each per-row variables menu
Findings.Impact: A long stepping session or browsing a large variable tree leaks a menu on each visible-row render, causing memory growth and making later menu-registry updates increasingly expensive.
Findings.Evidence: MenuService.createMenu returns a Menu that immediately subscribes to the global MenuRegistry.onDidChangeMenu and owns a RunOnceScheduler until Menu.dispose() is called. createAndFillInContextMenuActions disposes only the generated actions. AbstractExpressionsRenderer.disposeElement disposes only data.elementDisposable, where this code adds the actions but not menu. Thus the global registry retains every menu and its overlay after the row is recycled.
Findings.Recommendation: Add the created menu (and its per-row context service for lifecycle symmetry) to data.elementDisposable/one row DisposableStore before adding the generated actions, so disposeElement releases the registry subscription whenever the row is rerendered or recycled.

Scenarios.Scenario: Rendering, refreshing, scrolling, and opening context menus in the Debug Variables view
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A variables-tree refresh synchronously renders each visible variable row before the view is usable; each row now constructs an overlay, a DebugVariablesContext Menu, actions, and an ActionBar. Right-click additionally waits for dataBreakpointInfo only when the adapter supports data breakpoints before showing the menu.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: DAP variables request while expanding a variable or scope
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One request per uncached expanded container or chunk; large indexed collections are grouped into chunk nodes rather than fetched per item.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same cached/chunked variables request path existed before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Expansion waits for the request; ordinary row rendering does not issue it.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: DAP dataBreakpointInfo request before constructing a right-click variables menu
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one request per right-clicked variable when the session supports data breakpoints.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The old onContextMenu implementation also issued one awaited dataBreakpointInfo request per eligible right click.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The context menu waits for the adapter response.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Effective render cardinality is the virtualized visible-row count per refresh/scroll, repeated across debugger stops and row recycling; child loading is chunked at 100-based sizes and cached per ExpressionContainer until invalidated.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Row rendering and menu construction are synchronous on the UI thread. Variables/dataBreakpointInfo DAP requests are awaited by their individual expand/right-click workflows; no new concurrent boundary burst is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: ExpressionContainer coalesces child loads through its cached children Promise and chunks large indexed collections. Per-row menus are not cached and, because the new render path omits disposal, accumulate across row lifecycles. The explicit context-menu path correctly disposes its overlay and menu after use.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the added per-row createMenu call is on the synchronous render path, Menu subscribes to the global registry until disposed, and row disposal tracks only generated actions.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Viewport size, stop frequency, and session duration determine the leak rate; exact retained bytes per menu are not measured, but retention and unbounded lifecycle scaling are explicit.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable: every row render creates a globally retained menu that is omitted from row disposal, causing unbounded heap growth over long/debug-refresh-heavy sessions.

Scenarios.Scenario: Opening, reading, invalidating, and writing debugger memory through the hex editor filesystem provider
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The command checks extension availability, opens a virtual editor, and the consumer's reads/writes await the corresponding DAP readMemory/writeMemory response plus base64 conversion. Invalidation notifications are event-driven and off the initial open critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: DAP readMemory request followed by base64 decoding
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One adapter request per filesystem read; bytes equal the requested range after the consumer's chunking.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Debugger memory was not exposed through this filesystem path before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The hex view cannot display the requested bytes until the response is decoded.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: DAP writeMemory request after base64 encoding
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One adapter request per filesystem write, proportional in serialization size to bytes written.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Debugger memory writes were not available through this path before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The write waits for the adapter response before completion and invalidation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve/open the hex editor extension and virtual editor
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One extension lookup and one editor open per explicit View Memory command; revealIfOpened can reuse an existing editor.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Explicit user action waits for extension lookup and editor opening; if absent, it opens extension search instead.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Cost scales with bytes requested by the filesystem consumer and the number of read/write chunks. File descriptors scale with concurrently open virtual memory resources and are closed on editor close or session end.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Each provider read/write performs one awaited DAP operation; aggregate concurrency is controlled by the filesystem/hex-editor consumer, with no added loop or Promise.all burst in this diff.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: MemoryRegion has no byte cache: cold and repeated reads each reach the adapter. File descriptors map to regions and are removed on close/session end; invalidation listeners are disposed with regions.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for the one-DAP-call-per-provider-operation path; no evidence here establishes excessive cardinality because operations are demand-driven by the consumer.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The external hex editor's exact request chunk size and parallelism are outside this repository diff, so total request count for very large views is uncertain.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional finding: the remote boundary is the core requested feature, demand-driven rather than eager/per-item fan-out, and descriptor/listener cleanup is bounded by close or session end.

Scenarios.Scenario: Saving a base64 notebook output image to disk and opening it
Scenarios.CriticalPath: After the user selects a destination, base64 decoding, filesystem write, and opener invocation remain serial on the save action's critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same single write occurred after an atob plus byte-copy decode.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Opening the saved file waits for the write to finish.

ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same opener call existed before the diff.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: CPU and allocation scale linearly with encoded image bytes; there is one filesystem write and one open per explicit save.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Single user-triggered serial operation; no loop, fan-out, or new parallel burst.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache is used or needed for this one-shot conversion. The new decoder allocates one bounded output buffer and returns a view accounting for padding.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed path replaces, rather than adds to, decoding work and leaves boundary counts unchanged.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Real image sizes vary, but conversion remains byte-linear and removes the prior decoded-string-to-array copy loop.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: this is a bounded decoding optimization with unchanged filesystem/open cardinality.

Scenarios.Scenario: Debug service construction and virtual memory provider registration
Scenarios.CriticalPath: DebugService synchronously instantiates and registers the provider during service construction; registration itself does not perform adapter, filesystem, network, or subprocess work.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One provider per DebugService lifetime; open descriptors scale only after explicit memory editor use.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: No concurrent work is launched at registration.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The provider keeps only currently open descriptor-to-region entries and removes matching entries on session end.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: constructor work consists of map/emitter creation and an event subscription.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Provider construction cost is small and constant from inspected code.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: eager registration is constant and does not start heavyweight boundary work.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 21 changed files. One medium-confidence-independent, high-evidence memory regression was submitted: per-row variables menus are globally retained because the new render path never disposes them. Demand-driven debug-memory IPC, base64 serialization, provider lifecycle, startup registration, and notebook image saving showed no other actionable diff-introduced performance regression.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
